chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

“The mukātab is flogged, if he commits zina, in proportion to the amount of him that has been freed. But if he slanders a muḥṣanah, then he must be flogged eighty lashes, whether he is free or enslaved.”

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَةَ: a chaste woman protected from such accusation
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: a contracted slave working toward emancipation
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty lashes, the fixed hadd in this context
key_terms.قَذَفَ: slandered by accusing someone of zina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mukātab who commits zina or falsely accuses a chaste woman?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the punishment of a mukātab. It distinguishes between zina, where the punishment is proportionate to the degree of emancipation, and qadhf against a muḥṣanah, where the fixed punishment of eighty lashes applies whether the person is free or enslaved.
